1.title: Ensure Data Quality
1.text: Welcome to Module thirteen: Ensure Data Quality. This module covers the task statement: ensure data quality. Each part of this module comes from the study notes of the same name, so you can read the notes after you watch.

1.title: What You Will Learn
1.text: By the end of this module you will be able to do six things. Run data quality checks while processing data (for example empty fields). Define data quality rules with A W S Glue DataBrew (and A W S Glue Data Quality). Investigate data consistency. Describe data sampling techniques. Implement mechanisms for data skew. --.

1.title: Case Check-In: Kestrel Freight Trusts Its Numbers
1.text: Our running case is Kestrel Freight. Kestrel Freight Trusts Its Numbers. An invoice run billed a customer twice because of duplicate orders. Some trucks report temperature as −nine hundred ninety-nine and some weights as zero. Yesterday's file was half the usual size and nobody noticed. Your job: catch bad data before it reaches reports.

1.title: Dimensions of Data Quality
1.text: Dimensions of Data Quality. Completeness. Question: Is anything missing? Example check: shipment id is never null; at least ninety-five percent of customer id filled. Uniqueness. Question: Are there duplicates? Example check: shipment id unique. Validity. Question: Does it fit the allowed format, type or range? Example check: Weight between zero and forty thousand kg; date format; allowed status values. Accuracy. Question: Does it match reality? Example check: Delivered count equals the count in the source system. Consistency. Question: Do related values agree across fields, tables or systems? Example check: Delivery date is not before pickup date; source and target totals match. Timeliness (freshness). Question: Is it recent enough? Example check: Latest record is less than two hours old.

1.title: Dimensions of Data Quality, continued
1.text: Dimensions of Data Quality, continued. Integrity. Question: Do references resolve? Example check: Every customer id exists in the customer table. Volume. Question: Is the amount normal? Example check: Row count within plus or minus twenty percent of the usual. Exam tip: Match the problem to the dimension: nulls to completeness, duplicates to uniqueness, out-of-range to validity, source ≠ target to consistency, late data to timeliness.

1.title: Running Checks While Processing
1.text: Running Checks While Processing. The figure shows this: Quality gates in a pipeline: checks run while data is processed, good records continue to the curated zone, bad records are quarantined, and a failed gate raises an alert or stops the job. Check early and during processing, not only at the end: at ingestion, after each transformation, and before publishing. Where to run checks.

1.title: Running Checks While Processing, continued
1.text: Running Checks While Processing, continued. A W S Glue E T L (extract, transform, load) jobs. A W S Glue Data Quality (the EvaluateDataQuality transform with a ruleset) or Spark code (filter, counts, null checks). A W S Glue Data Catalog tables. Glue Data Quality rulesets run on a schedule or on demand against a table. A W S Glue DataBrew. Rulesets and profile jobs (visual). A W S Lambda. Small, event-driven validation of an arriving file. Athena or Redshift S Q L. Set-based checks (count, where col is null, group by... having count() greater than one). Streaming. Flink or Lambda validate records; bad records go to a dead-letter destination.

1.title: Running Checks While Processing, continued
1.text: Running Checks While Processing, continued. What to do with a failure (choose by severity):; Fail the job and alert (a critical rule broke); Quarantine the bad records to a rejected S three prefix or D L Q (dead-letter queue) with the reason, and continue with the good ones; Fix automatically (default values, standardization) and log the change; Alert only (a warning rule). Examples of checks: empty fields, schema match, data types, ranges, uniqueness, referential integrity, row counts, freshness.

1.title: AWS Glue Data Quality
1.text: A W S Glue Data Quality. Define rules in D Q D L (Data Quality Definition Language) (Data Quality Definition Language), evaluate them in E T L jobs or on catalog tables, get a quality score and rule-by-rule results (to the console, S three, CloudWatch and EventBridge). Built on the open-source Deequ; Glue can recommend rules from the data.

1.title: AWS Glue Data Quality, continued
1.text: A W S Glue Data Quality, continued. The example is on the screen; read it line by line when you study. Exam tip: "Stop the job or route bad rows to a quarantine when required fields are empty" to Glue Data Quality rules in the job, with bad records written to a rejected location and an alert.

1.title: Defining Data Quality Rules with DataBrew
1.text: Defining Data Quality Rules with DataBrew. The figure shows this: DataBrew data quality rules: profile a dataset, define a ruleset of checks and thresholds, run a profile job, and review the validation results. A W S Glue DataBrew profiles data and applies data quality rules without code. Profile job: computes statistics per column: missing values, distinct count, duplicates, min, max, mean, distribution, correlations, outliers.

1.title: Defining Data Quality Rules with DataBrew, continued
1.text: Defining Data Quality Rules with DataBrew, continued. Ruleset: a named set of rules attached to a dataset; each rule has checks (conditions on a column or the whole dataset), thresholds (for example fail if more than five percent missing) and a severity. Typical checks: column is not null, values within a range or list, column value matches a pattern, uniqueness, row count, column statistics, data type. Validation results (pass or fail per rule) are written to S three, and a failed ruleset can stop or alert the pipeline; run on a schedule.

1.title: Defining Data Quality Rules with DataBrew, continued
1.text: Defining Data Quality Rules with DataBrew, continued. Pick the tool: DataBrew for visual, analyst-owned rules; Glue Data Quality (D Q D L) for engineer-owned rules inside jobs and catalogs.

1.title: Investigating Data Consistency
1.text: Investigating Data Consistency. Consistency means the same facts agree across fields, records, tables and systems, and over time. Investigate with:; Profiling (DataBrew profile job): duplicates, missing values, correlations, odd distributions; Reconciliation queries: compare counts, sums, min and max (or hashes) between source and target; Cross-field rules: delivered date greater than equals pickup date; totals equal the sum of lines; Referential checks: orphan keys with a left join; Glue Data Quality dataset checks: compare two datasets; A W S D M S (Database Migration Service) data validation: compares rows in source and target after a migration or replication and reports mismatches.

1.title: Investigating Data Consistency, continued
1.text: Investigating Data Consistency, continued. System-level consistency to know:; Amazon S three provides strong read-after-write consistency for object writes, overwrites and deletes and for listings; DynamoDB: reads are eventually consistent by default; request a strongly consistent read when you must see the latest write (not available on global secondary indexes); transactions give all-or-nothing writes; Distributed pipelines: at-least-once delivery causes duplicates, so idempotent writes and de-duplication keep data consistent; Apache Iceberg and transactions give atomic commits to lake tables. Fixing inconsistency: find the source of truth, correct upstream, reprocess (idempotently), add a rule so it is caught next time. Exam tip: "After migrating, prove source and target match" to A W S D M S data validation (plus row-count and checksum comparisons).

1.title: Data Sampling Techniques
1.text: Data Sampling Techniques. Sampling takes a subset of data to profile, test or check it quickly and cheaply instead of scanning everything. Techniques.

2.title: Data Sampling Techniques, continued
2.text: Data Sampling Techniques, continued. Simple random. How: Every row has equal chance. Use it when: General profiling; avoids bias. Systematic. How: Every n-th row. Use it when: Ordered data, fast and simple (watch for hidden patterns). Stratified. How: Sample within each group (route, region) in proportion. Use it when: Rare groups must be represented. Cluster. How: Pick whole groups (a partition or file) at random. Use it when: Cheap when reading whole files. Reservoir. How: Keep a fixed-size random sample of a stream of unknown length. Use it when: Streaming data. First-N (head). How: Take the first rows. Use it when: Quick look only: may be biased.

2.title: Data Sampling Techniques, continued
2.text: Data Sampling Techniques, continued. In A W S: DataBrew profile jobs can use the full dataset or a sample (for example the first N rows or a random N rows); Athena T A B L E S A M P L E and Spark sample() for random subsets; Glue Data Quality and Spark jobs can run on a sample to save cost. Cautions: a sample can miss rare errors and can be biased; use bigger or stratified samples for rare events and run full checks for critical rules.

2.title: Data Skew
2.text: Data Skew. The figure shows this: Data skew: an uneven key distribution gives one worker most of the work, so the job waits for that straggler; salting or repartitioning spreads the load. Data skew equals values are not evenly spread: one key holds a large share of the rows, so one partition, node, shard or task does most of the work (a straggler) or runs out of memory.

2.title: Data Skew, continued
2.text: Data Skew, continued. Symptoms: one task much slower in the Spark U I; one Kinesis shard or DynamoDB partition throttled while others idle; one Redshift slice holds many more rows; out-of-memory on one executor. Mechanisms to handle skew.

2.title: Data Skew, continued
2.text: Data Skew, continued. Spark (Glue, E M R (Elastic MapReduce)). Salting: add a random suffix to the hot key, aggregate in two steps; repartition on a better key; broadcast the small side of a join; enable adaptive query execution skew-join handling; filter hot or null keys and process them separately. Redshift. Choose a distribution key with many distinct, evenly used values; use even or auto; check skew in table information views; avoid a key with many nulls. DynamoDB. High-cardinality partition key, or a suffix (write sharding) for very hot keys; spread keys.

2.title: Data Skew, continued
2.text: Data Skew, continued. Kinesis or Kafka. Partition key with many values; add a random suffix for hot keys; split the hot shard or use on-demand. S three or Athena. Partition by a balanced column; avoid a few giant partitions; compact small files. Exam tip: "One task runs for hours while the rest finish in seconds after a join on customer id, and one customer has most rows" to data skew: salt the key, broadcast, or enable adaptive skew handling.

2.title: Module Recap
2.text: Here is the recap. Dimensions: Completeness, uniqueness, validity, accuracy, consistency, timeliness, integrity, volume. Checks in processing: Early and repeated. D Q D L: Rules equals [ IsComplete "col", Uniqueness "col" greater than zero point nine nine, ColumnValues "col" between a and b, RowCount greater than n ]; built on Deequ; score and results to S three or CloudWatch or EventBridge. DataBrew: Profile job (missing, duplicates, distribution, outliers), ruleset with checks, thresholds, severity, validation results in S three. Consistency: Profile, reconcile counts or sums or hashes, cross-field and referential rules, D M S data validation; S three strong consistency. Sampling: Random, systematic, stratified, cluster, reservoir (streams), first-N (biased); Athena T A B L E S A M P L E, Spark sample(). Skew: One hot key to straggler.

2.title: Practice Question 1
2.text: Question one. During an A W S Glue job the team must stop processing and alert when required fields such as shipment id are empty, and route other invalid records for review. What is the best design? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B. Quality rules in the job detect problems early, quarantining isolates bad records with the reason, and alerts notify the team.

2.title: Practice Question 2
2.text: Question two. Analysts without coding skills want to define data quality checks such as "no more than five percent missing values in the weight column" and review pass or fail results. Which service should they use? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A. DataBrew provides visual data quality rules with thresholds and validation results without code.

2.title: Practice Question 3
2.text: Question three. Select two. After a database migration the team must confirm that the rows in the target match the source. Which two actions help? The five options are on the screen. The answers are B and D. D M S data validation compares source and target rows, and count and checksum comparisons confirm consistency. The other actions do not verify data.

2.title: Practice Question 4
2.text: Question four. Select two. A join on customer id makes one Spark task run for hours because a single customer has most of the rows. Which two actions reduce the problem? The five options are on the screen. The answers are D and E. Uneven key distribution is data skew; salting the hot key and adaptive skew-join handling spread the work across tasks. Small files, no partitioning and dropping the join do not fix the imbalance.

2.title: Practice Question 5
2.text: Question five. A team wants to profile a very large dataset quickly and cheaply and make sure rare categories are represented. Which sampling technique is best? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B. Stratified sampling samples within each group, so rare categories are represented; the first rows can be biased.

2.title: Answers at a Glance
2.text: Here are all five answers. Question one: B. Question two: A. Question three: B and D. Question four: D and E. Question five: B. In the next module, we continue the course.
